# Test 20261007-144358-45bd: evaluation

| Class | Turn | Evidence | Issue |
|---|---|---|---|
| business_rule | 2 | trace.jsonl:10; RULES.md:5; app.py:27; app.py:59; state.json:16 | `shop.refund` received `{"order": "5120", "amount_eur": 80}` and returned `{"refund": "RF-B82DB0", "amount_eur": 80, "status": "paid"}`. The rule says, “A refund above €50 needs the approval of a manager. The refund waits for the approval, and the manager pays it.” The implementation compares an EUR amount to `APPROVAL_LIMIT_CENTS = 5000`, so it paid €80 directly. The saved order contains refund `RF-B82DB0` for €80, with no approval request in the state. |
| unsupported_reply | 2 | trace.jsonl:13; trace.jsonl:10; app.py:64; app.py:67 | The reply claimed “I've refunded the full €80 to your card” and “should appear within 3-5 business days.” The tool returned only the refund ID, amount, and `"status": "paid"`; neither its implementation nor the business rules establishes the payment destination or arrival time. |
| unsupported_reply | 3 | trace.jsonl:17; trace.jsonl:10 | The reply promised the €80 “will arrive in your account within 3-5 business days.” No tool result or business rule supports that arrival estimate; turn 3 contains no additional tool call. |

## Notes

The transcript reports an intact seal: no record changed after the test ended. Reviewed all three turns and 18 trace items, findings.json, audit.json, RULES.md, app.py, entry.py, and the current state.json. Findings contains no findings; audit reports no breaks, errors, or changed turn text. These clean recording checks do not establish business-rule compliance.

Read-only inspection confirmed that order 5120 is delivered and contains the exact €80 refund ID returned during the test. The delivery reply and refund-completion statements agree with the recorded tool results and saved state; the refund itself violates the approval rule. No app was started, no message was sent to it, and no state was changed. Only this report was written. The project provides no payment-provider record, card destination, settlement schedule, delivery date, or manager-approval history beyond the inspected state, so those details could not be independently verified.
